text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Stocks snapped a three-day winning streak, shrugging off fresh Wall Street gains as investors fretted about interest rates, inflation and the impact of sterling strength on company earnings. The FTSE 100 index closed down 15.3 points at 3,962.8 in modest volume of around 635 million shares.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended bourse dealings higher, after Wall Street hit yet another record high, but gains were capped as a jump in a German business climate index undermined rate cut hopes. The 30-share DAX index ended up 10.41 points at 2,774.50. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 2,766.36.

PARIS - Stocks finished lower but above their session lows after the bourse took heart from an early advance on Wall Street to new highs. The bourse's weak tone was set early by the German Ifo index signalling greater than expected business confidence in the German economy, and it sank further in the afternoon on a larger than expected U.S. trade deficit for September. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 6.66 points at 2,233.39.

ZURICH - Shares closed lower on profit-taking after hitting new highs earlier in the session. Selling in major pharmaceuticals Roche, Ciba and Sandoz as well as Nestle weighed on the market. Wall Street shares lost steam after a strong beginning which also pressured Swiss indices. The broad SPI ended down 4.86 points, or 0.2 percent, at 2,481.69 points.

TOKYO - The stock market's key benchmark ended more than one percent higher after both domestic and institutional investors moved to buy blue-chip issues, extending early morning gains inspired by a record high close on Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 closed 233.78 points or 1.12 percent higher at 21,189.96.

HONG KONG - Stocks marched to a record close for the third consecutive day, boosted by a positive outlook for lending rates and the potential impact of that scenario on the market's chief sectors. The Hang Seng Index held onto a gain of 110.23 points to set a record close of 13,167.16.
SYDNEY - Shares sprinted home to a record close as an afternoon rally pushed an already Dow-inspired market to higher territory. The All Ordinaries index rose 26.7 points to close at 2,392.7.

JOHANNESBURG - As the bullion price hopped above $379 an ounce, gold shares braved a break from the tight range they held throughout the day's trade and added 1.5 percent to the value of their index. Having straddled their opening levels for most of the day, the slight strengthening in the gold price gave metal shares the courage to move up and finish 25.3 points higher at 1,712.5. Industrial stocks lost 9.6 points to 8,077.3 and the all-share index slipped to 6,850.9 -- 15.1 points down.
